query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix, whose overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures remain unclear, what single intervention could improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions, defines the operating limits of the prediction, cites supporting evidence from the introduction, and proposes a falsification experiment capable of resolving microscopic deformation during wear.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix can be improved by refining its grain size.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix
generation.conditions: Sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths
generation.mechanism: The fine grain size provides higher surface strength and hardness, which improves wear resistance. Under friction heat, coarse grain samples soften more easily, causing their oxide layers to fracture and leading to increased wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance compared to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to high temperatures; friction velocities: low to high; wear depths: low to high
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between grain size and wear resistance in the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating is unclear and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of wear resistance between fine-grained and coarse-grained FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coatings under various sliding conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the fine-grained coating does not exhibit improved wear resistance compared to the coarse-grained coating under the specified conditions, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does grain size influence the tribological behavior, wear mechanisms, and wear resistance of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloys under varying normal loads and sliding speeds?. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) with fine grain (FG, ~2.9 μm) and coarse grain (CG, ~63.4 μm) microstructures. Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals followed by drop-casting into a copper mold, forging at 1000 °C, cold rolling (80% reduction), and annealing at 800 °C for 30 min (FG) or 1000 °C for 60 min (CG). Test conditions: Reciprocating sliding friction against a 10 mm Si3N4 ball under dry conditions at room temperature; normal loads of 5 N and 30 N; sliding speeds of 1, 5, and 10 mm/s; sliding time of 1200 s.
